bill.title: FAIR Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Hospitals receiving Medicare GME payments face new reporting requirements and potential payment reductions for noncompliance.
Medical schools (both osteopathic and allopathic) are directly affected by transparency requirements around residency acceptance rates.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires hospitals that receive Medicare graduate medical education payments to report how many residency applicants come from osteopathic versus allopathic medical schools, how many from each group are accepted, and to confirm they consider both types of applicants equally. Hospitals that fail to report this information would see their Medicare education payments reduced by 2%. The data would be posted publicly online.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services of the Department of Health and Human Services relating to "Medicare Program; Implementation of Prior Authorization for Select Services for the Wasteful and Inappropriate Services Reduction (WISeR) Model".
bill.latestActionText: Motion to proceed to consideration of measure rejected in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 46 - 50. Record Vote Number: 199.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The prior authorization model directly affects hospitals and physician groups by requiring advance approval for certain Medicare services they provide.
Third-party contractors processing prior authorization requests are typically health insurers or related entities that would lose revenue from this model's termination.
The model specifically requires enhanced technology and artificial intelligence systems for processing authorization requests, affecting technology vendors serving the healthcare sector.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Medicare pilot program that began in January 2026 in six states. The program requires third-party contractors to use enhanced technology, including artificial intelligence, to review and approve certain Medicare services before they are provided. The contractors are paid based on a share of any savings generated. This resolution would stop the program from continuing.

bill.title: Rural Development Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets rural hospitals, providing them with technical assistance, training, and support for operational and financial improvements.
The program explicitly includes increasing telehealth capabilities as a development need, which would affect broadband and telecommunications infrastructure providers serving rural hospitals.
The bill addresses acquiring and upgrading health care information systems including electronic health records, which would involve technology vendors and IT service providers.
The program covers technical assistance for constructing, expanding, and modernizing health care facilities, which would involve construction and engineering firms.

bill.plainSummary: This bill formally establishes a technical assistance program within the Department of Agriculture to help rural hospitals (in areas with 50,000 or fewer residents) improve their operations and finances. The program would provide training and support to help these hospitals modernize facilities, expand telehealth, upgrade information systems, and navigate USDA loan and grant programs. Priority would go to hospitals already participating in certain USDA rural assistance programs, and USDA would report annually to Congress on the program's results.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Benton MacKaye National Scenic Trail Feasibility Study Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 211.

industries.rationale: National scenic trail designation could affect tourism and outdoor recreation businesses near the trail corridor.
Federal trail designation may impose land-use restrictions or affect property values along the 287-mile corridor.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Forest Service to conduct a study examining whether the Benton MacKaye Trail should be designated as a national scenic trail. The trail runs approximately 287 miles through Georgia, Tennessee, and North Carolina. The study would assess the feasibility of granting the trail this federal designation.

plain.whoItTouches: People who visit public land, and people who live beside it.
